$$
\begin{aligned}4{p}^{2}+21p & =3{p}^{2}+2{p}^{3} \\ -2{p}^{3}+4{p}^{2}+21p & =3{p}^{2} \\ -2{p}^{3}+{p}^{2}+21p & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Next, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $-p.$ We can factor out the $-p$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{p}^{3}+{p}^{2}+21p & =0 \\ -p(2{p}^{2}-p-21) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression $2{p}^{2}-p-21$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-p(2{p}^{2}-p-21) & =0 \\ -p(2p-7)(p+3) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $p=0,$ $p=\frac{7}{2},$ and $p=-3.$

questions.problem: Determine the solutions of the equation $10{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}=\frac{9}{2}x-10{x}^{2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the polynomial equation in the form ${P}_{n}(x)=0.$ To do this, we subtract all the terms from the right-hand side so that the right-hand side becomes $0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}10{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2} & =\frac{9}{2}x-10{x}^{2} \\ 10{x}^{3}+12{x}^{2} & =\frac{9}{2}x \\ 10{x}^{3}+12{x}^{2}-\frac{9}{2}x & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we can factor out the $\frac{x}{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}10{x}^{3}+12{x}^{2}-\frac{9}{2}x & =0 \\ \frac{x}{2}(20{x}^{2}+24x-9) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression $20{x}^{2}+24x-9$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2}(20{x}^{2}+24x-9) & =0 \\ \frac{x}{2}(10x-3)(2x+3) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $x=0,$ $x=\frac{3}{10},$ and $x=-\frac{3}{2}.$

questions.problem: Find the roots of the polynomial $p(y)=8{y}^{4}+4{y}^{3}-12{y}^{2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the roots of the polynomial, we must solve the equation $p(y)=0,$ that is

$$
8{y}^{4}+4{y}^{3}-12{y}^{2}=0.
$$

First, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $4{y}^{2}.$ We can factor out the $4{y}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{y}^{2}(2{y}^{2}+y-3) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression $2{y}^{2}+y-3$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{y}^{2}(2{y}^{2}+y-3) & =0 \\ 4{y}^{2}(2y+3)(y-1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $y=0,$ $y=-\frac{3}{2},$ and $y=1.$

questions.problem: Find the roots of the polynomial $p(q)=24{q}^{5}-62{q}^{4}+14{q}^{3}.$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the roots of the polynomial, we must solve the equation $p(q)=0,$ that is

$$
24{q}^{5}-62{q}^{4}+14{q}^{3}=0.
$$

First, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $2{q}^{3}.$ We can factor out the $2{q}^{3}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{q}^{3}(12{q}^{2}-31q+7) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression $12{q}^{2}-31q+7$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{q}^{3}(12{q}^{2}-31q+7) & =0 \\ 2{q}^{3}(4q-1)(3q-7) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $q=0,$ $q=\frac{1}{4},$ and $q=\frac{7}{3}.$
